learningOutcomes: Create and modify a perpendicular structural framing column using an explicit cross-section, anchor point and plane-based height.
Assign representation, material, trade, calculation mode and classification data required for downstream schedules and exchange checks.
Verify the column workflow without treating software output as structural design approval.
prerequisites: Allplan 2026 workspace with the Structural Framing task available in the installed license.
A project building structure and plane model whose story elevations have already been checked.
p3-c1-m1.interfaceContext: Architecture role > Structural Framing task > Structural Framing Objects > Structural Framing Column

stepsEvidence.title: Open Structural Framing Column and define geometry
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: The Geometry tab shows the agreed cross-section, dimensions and anchor point.

stepsEvidence.title: Bind top and bottom levels to the checked plane model
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: The Height dialog shows explicit top and bottom plane references and the preview is placed in the correct story.

stepsEvidence.title: Assign attributes and verify downstream classification
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: Material, trade, calculation mode and classification are visible and the agreed exchange check identifies the object as IfcColumn.

p3-c1-m1.learnerOutput: One modelled structural framing column with reproducible geometry, plane-based height, attribute data and an IfcColumn verification result.

checkpoint.prompt: Submit the three workstation screenshots and the agreed IfcColumn verification result for the created object.
checkpoint.acceptanceCriteria: Geometry, plane references, attributes and exchange classification must match the reviewed evidence pack.

assessmentQuestion.prompt: Which settings must be verified before a structural framing column can be trusted in schedules and IFC exchange?
assessmentQuestion.expectedAnswer: Cross-section and anchor point, top and bottom plane references, material and trade, calculation mode, attributes and the resulting IfcColumn classification.

learningOutcomes: Create a horizontal or inclined structural framing beam with an explicit cross-section, construction method and anchor-point geometry.
Verify height behavior and downstream classification without confusing software output with structural design approval.
Record the beam attributes and exchange result required for a reproducible review.
prerequisites: ALLPLAN 2026 workspace with the Structural Framing task available in the installed license.
A checked building structure and plane model with agreed story elevations.
p3-c1-m2.interfaceContext: Architecture role > Structural Framing task > Structural Framing Objects > Structural Framing Beam

stepsEvidence.title: Open Structural Framing Beam and define geometry
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: The Geometry tab shows the agreed cross-section, construction method, dimensions and start anchor point.

stepsEvidence.title: Place the beam and verify its height behavior
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: The start and end anchor points and the horizontal or inclined height settings match the checked model context.

stepsEvidence.title: Assign attributes and verify exchange classification
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: The agreed attributes are visible and the exchange check identifies the structural framing beam as IfcBeam.

p3-c1-m2.learnerOutput: One reproducible structural framing beam with reviewed geometry, height behavior, attributes and an IfcBeam verification result.

checkpoint.prompt: Submit the three workstation screenshots and the agreed IfcBeam verification result for the created object.
checkpoint.acceptanceCriteria: Geometry, construction method, anchor points, height behavior, attributes and exchange classification must match the reviewed evidence pack.

assessmentQuestion.prompt: Which beam settings and outputs must be verified before the object can be trusted in schedules and IFC exchange?
assessmentQuestion.expectedAnswer: Cross-section, construction method, start and end anchor points, plane or height behavior, attributes and the resulting IfcBeam classification.

learningOutcomes: Model a wall with explicit construction layers, axis and plane-based height settings in the checked building structure.
Distinguish wall geometry and IFC classification from structural-capacity approval.
Verify layer terminations and exchange classification using reproducible evidence.
prerequisites: ALLPLAN 2026 workspace with the Architecture role and wall tools available.
A checked building structure and plane model with agreed story elevations.
p3-c1-m3.interfaceContext: Architecture role > Elements task > Wall, with Building Structure and Plane Model context

stepsEvidence.title: Define wall layers, thicknesses and component axis
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: The wall parameters show the reviewed layer order, material context, thicknesses and component axis.

stepsEvidence.title: Bind wall-layer heights to checked reference planes
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: Layer heights and any slab offset visibly reference the agreed upper or lower planes.

stepsEvidence.title: Verify wall geometry and IFC classification
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: The wall is present in the intended drawing-file context and the exchange check reports the reviewed IfcWallStandardCase or IfcWall classification.

p3-c1-m3.learnerOutput: One reproducible layered wall with reviewed axis, plane-based heights and an explicit IFC wall classification result.

references.title: ALLPLAN 2026-1 Multilayer walls with different height settings
ALLPLAN 2026-1 Shortcut menu of building structure

checkpoint.prompt: Submit the three workstation screenshots and the agreed IFC wall-classification result.
checkpoint.acceptanceCriteria: Layer order, axis, plane references, offsets and exchange classification must match the reviewed evidence pack.

assessmentQuestion.prompt: Which evidence distinguishes a correctly coordinated wall model from an unsupported claim of structural adequacy?
assessmentQuestion.expectedAnswer: Reviewed wall layers and axis, plane-based heights and offsets, drawing-file context and IFC classification prove model coordination; structural capacity still requires engineering analysis and approval.

learningOutcomes: Organize reviewed structural model elements in the Building Structure with explicit drawing-file and plane assignments.
Generate an auditable model report without presenting modeled quantities as structural-capacity verification.
Identify the boundary between coordinated physical-model data and engineering analysis.
prerequisites: ALLPLAN 2026 project with modeled columns, beams, walls and slabs.
A checked story hierarchy and plane model.
p3-c2-m1.interfaceContext: Open on a Project-Specific Basis > Building Structure and Plane Model, plus Reports

stepsEvidence.title: Organize structural elements by structural level and drawing file
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: The Building Structure shows the reviewed hierarchy and drawing-file assignments.

stepsEvidence.title: Assign and verify reference planes
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: The selected structural level and drawing files show the agreed plane assignments and elevations.

stepsEvidence.title: Generate and reconcile a component report
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: A report lists reviewed model objects and quantities that reconcile with the selected drawing-file scope.

p3-c2-m1.learnerOutput: A reproducible Building Structure selection with checked planes and a scoped component report, explicitly marked as non-analytical.

references.title: ALLPLAN 2026-1 Creating a building structure automatically
ALLPLAN 2026-1 Shortcut menu of building structure

checkpoint.prompt: Submit the three workstation screenshots and reconcile the report scope to the reviewed model selection.
checkpoint.acceptanceCriteria: Hierarchy, drawing files, planes and report objects must match; the output must not claim structural-capacity approval.

assessmentQuestion.prompt: What does a coordinated Building Structure and component report prove, and what does it not prove?
assessmentQuestion.expectedAnswer: It proves model organization, scope and entered geometry or quantities; it does not prove loads, load paths, resistance, stability or code compliance.

learningOutcomes: Create and name a reproducible axis grid with explicit x, y and z spacing and reviewed labels.
Modify grid axes without silently breaking numbering or member-alignment checks.
Verify `IfcGrid` exchange classification while keeping structural layout approval outside the software workflow.
prerequisites: ALLPLAN 2026 workspace with Axis Grid available.
An approved project coordinate, origin and structural grid schedule.
p3-c2-m2.interfaceContext: Draft role > Design task > Grid area, or Structural Framing module > Axis Grid

stepsEvidence.title: Define x and y grid geometry and labels
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: The Axis Grid palette shows the reviewed origin, rotation, x/y spacings and label sequences.

stepsEvidence.title: Configure z-direction planes and place the grid
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: The placed grid shows the agreed z-direction copies and retains its reviewed grid name.

stepsEvidence.title: Verify member alignment and IFC grid classification
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: A checked view records grid-to-member alignment and the exchange result identifies the 3D grid as IfcGrid.

p3-c2-m2.learnerOutput: One named and reproducible 3D axis grid with checked spacing, labels, member-alignment evidence and an IfcGrid verification result.

checkpoint.prompt: Submit the three workstation screenshots and reconcile the grid schedule, placed axes and IFC result.
checkpoint.acceptanceCriteria: Origin, rotation, spacings, labels, z-levels and IfcGrid classification must match the approved grid schedule.

assessmentQuestion.prompt: Which grid changes can create coordination risk even when the axis object remains valid?
assessmentQuestion.expectedAnswer: Changes to origin, rotation, spacing, z-levels, numbering or custom labels can misalign members and references; each requires a renewed coordination check.

learningOutcomes: Configure a scoped IFC export with explicit schema, view definition, drawing files, unit and coordinate settings.
Apply and verify attribute mapping without silently dropping required properties.
Validate the exported IFC independently instead of treating file creation as proof of quality.
prerequisites: A reviewed ALLPLAN 2026 structural model and agreed exchange requirements.
An approved IFC schema, Model View Definition, coordinate basis and property requirement set.
p3-c3-m1.interfaceContext: Draft role > Teamwork task > Export > Export IFC Data > Exchange profile settings

stepsEvidence.title: Select IFC schema, view definition and export scope
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: The export dialog shows the approved file type, MVD, drawing files and element filters.

stepsEvidence.title: Verify coordinates, units and attribute mapping
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: Unit, scale, project offset and active CFG mapping match the exchange requirements.

stepsEvidence.title: Validate the exported IFC independently
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: An independent check records schema, coordinates, entity counts and required property presence.

p3-c3-m1.learnerOutput: One versioned IFC export plus an independent validation record covering scope, coordinates, entities and required properties.

checkpoint.prompt: Submit the export-configuration screenshots, resulting IFC and independent validation evidence.
checkpoint.acceptanceCriteria: Schema, scope, coordinates, entities and required properties must match the approved exchange requirements.

assessmentQuestion.prompt: Why is a successfully written IFC file insufficient evidence of a valid structural export?
assessmentQuestion.expectedAnswer: The file can still have wrong scope, units, offsets, entities or missing properties; these require independent semantic and coordinate validation.

learningOutcomes: Convert a reviewed physical structural model into an explicit analytical-model draft.
Review element roles, system lines, eccentricities, connectivity and material/profile mappings.
Separate model preparation from supports, loading, combinations, solver checks and engineering approval.
prerequisites: A reviewed ALLPLAN 2026 structural model and agreed analysis scope.
Access to ALLPLAN AutoConverter and the target analysis application.
p3-c3-m2.interfaceContext: ALLPLAN/Bimplus structural model > ALLPLAN AutoConverter > target structural analysis application

stepsEvidence.title: Review recognized elements and analytical roles
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: Included elements, removed non-loadbearing objects and analytical roles match the approved analysis scope.

stepsEvidence.title: Resolve alignment, connectivity and section mappings
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: System lines, eccentricities, master planes, connections, profiles and materials have reviewed mappings.

stepsEvidence.title: Validate the analytical draft in the target application
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: The target application records connectivity and model diagnostics before loads or design results are accepted.

p3-c3-m2.learnerOutput: One traceable analytical-model draft with documented exclusions, role mappings, alignment decisions and target-tool diagnostics.

checkpoint.prompt: Submit recognition, alignment and target-tool diagnostic evidence for the analytical-model draft.
checkpoint.acceptanceCriteria: Scope, roles, exclusions, system lines, mappings and connectivity diagnostics must match the structural review.

assessmentQuestion.prompt: Why can a converted analytical model not be treated as a validated FEM model?
assessmentQuestion.expectedAnswer: Conversion does not prove connectivity, supports, loads, combinations, mesh quality, solver behavior, resistance checks or code compliance.

learningOutcomes: Generate a scoped structural view in a controlled Building Structure drawing file.
Verify model references, axes, scale, representation and annotations before issue.
Distinguish associative generation from approved construction documentation.
prerequisites: A reviewed ALLPLAN 2026 model and Building Structure.
An approved drawing register, scale and issue-status convention.
p3-c4-m1.interfaceContext: Building Structure > Derived from building structure > Views > Generate View

stepsEvidence.title: Assign source and output drawing files
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: The Building Structure shows the reviewed model scope and dedicated output drawing file.

stepsEvidence.title: Generate the structural view
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: View direction, scale, representation, clipping and axis settings match the drawing register.

stepsEvidence.title: Review the drawing output for issue
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: The output records checked axes, dimensions, labels, references, revision and issue status.

p3-c4-m1.learnerOutput: One derived structural view with traceable source files and a completed drawing-review record.

references.title: ALLPLAN 2026-1 Creating views in Building Structure

checkpoint.prompt: Submit source/output scope, generation settings and reviewed drawing evidence.
checkpoint.acceptanceCriteria: Scope, scale, axes, representation, annotation, revision and issue status must match the drawing register.

assessmentQuestion.prompt: Why is an associative view not automatically an approved structural drawing?
assessmentQuestion.expectedAnswer: Association updates model geometry but does not approve scope, scale, dimensions, annotations, detailing, revisions or construction issue status.

learningOutcomes: Define a traceable clipping path, viewing direction and vertical extent for a structural section.
Verify source drawing-file scope and model references before generating output.
Review section intersections, axes, annotations and revision status before issue.
prerequisites: A reviewed ALLPLAN 2026 structural model and Building Structure.
An approved section register with identifiers, locations and view directions.
p3-c4-m2.interfaceContext: Architecture role > Elements task > Views and Sections > Clipping Path and Generate Section

stepsEvidence.title: Define clipping path and viewing direction
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: Section identifier, clipping outline and viewing direction match the approved section register.

stepsEvidence.title: Set vertical extent and source scope
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: Top/bottom levels or height-from-elements and referenced drawing files are explicit and reviewed.

stepsEvidence.title: Generate and review the section output
stepsEvidence.expectedOutput: The section records checked axes, cut elements, intersections, dimensions, labels, revision and issue status.

p3-c4-m2.learnerOutput: One generated structural section with traceable clipping geometry, source scope and completed output review.
